perspectives.title: WWII Veterans
perspectives.summary: Most people did not live through WWII

representative_posts.author: taupress.com
representative_posts.text: I'm 68 - I did not live through WWII. It had been over for 13 years by the time I was born. Even the final bits of rationing had been gone for at least 5 years.

representative_posts.author: simonziegler.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My parents were 9 and 20 when the war ended. Dad was in the RAF. To be clear, they both firmly held open welcoming views and were pro EU, and part of this was a specific reaction of WWII. I think their generation were more pro EU in 2016 than those who didn’t experience the war.

perspectives.title: WWII Veterans
perspectives.summary: Most people who lived through WWII are no longer alive

representative_posts.author: teaforpterosaur.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: My nan was 14 when she worked in the parachute factory in WWII and she would now be 101 if she hadn't died in 2010 so I'm just wondering how many people who "lived through the war" are still about ringing the Daily Mail to complain about black people

representative_posts.author: robod99.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: There are roughly 3100 men over the age of 100 in the UK. Anyone younger is too young to be a WWII veteran. Can we stop pretending there is this vast cohort of WWII heroes who are disappointed we are not following the Nazi example. It is wrong on all levels.

representative_posts.author: redcirclefp.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Anyone who fought in WW2 is at least 98/9

representative_posts.author: athenepallas.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: Were he still alive, my late father would be 96, born in 1930: he was therefore of an age to remember the war (he was an evacuee). However, a great many people who *think* of themselves as having 'lived through war' are actually much younger than that.

representative_posts.author: mjpm69.bsky.social
representative_posts.text: The generation that “lived through war” would have to be at least 81 years old (older to have any memory of the war). That’s less than 2% of the population. These people aren’t the bulk of those supporting Farage.
